ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), SC 2000, c. 17, and regulations thereunder; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c. C-46, Part II.1; United Nations Act, SC 1991, c. 45; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c. 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2017, c. 21; Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.); Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c. B-9, including the Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register regime; FINTRAC directives and guidance on customer due diligence and politically exposed persons.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport or national identity card of each director, officer, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of the individual or the issuing government authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (where the issuing state is an Apostille Convention party; Canada recognizes such apostilles effective 11 January 2024) or Canadian consular legalization if the issuing state is not a party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (recent utility bill, bank statement, or government-issued address certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank or utility company / municipal authorities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution maintaining the funding account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signing officer attestation with apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or certificate of incorporation of any corporate UBO / shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or consular legalization through the foreign ministry / consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly notarized power of attorney or authorization for the Alberta registered agent and filing representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the principal's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization as applicable) and certified English translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of each UBO, director, officer, and authorized representative against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list; Canadian sanctions regulations under the United Nations Act and Special Economic Measures Act; FINTRAC politically exposed persons categories (domestic, foreign, and international organization) per PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance; OFAC SDN list and US secondary sanctions risk indicators; UK HM Treasury sanctions list; and publicly available negative media/corruption registries. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, family member, close associate, litigation, insolvency, civil forfeiture, adverse media, unusual purchase-payment patterns, or sourcing from high-risk mineral supply jurisdictions. Mandatory Suspicious Transaction Reports to FINTRAC are required as applicable.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) - Corporate Name Search and NUANS (Newly Upgraded Name Search) via authorized registry agents or the official OneStop Alberta corporate registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be in Latin letters; English and French are both accepted. Alberta corporations are not required to use a French legal element, but the legal ending must be one of the prescribed elements such as 'Inc.', 'Ltd.', 'Corp.', 'Incorporated', or 'Limitée'. Chinese characters are not accepted for the statutory corporate name; a trade name may be registered separately in transliteration provided it is not confusingly similar to existing names, and all non-English/French words must be accompanied by an English or French translation in the NUANS submission.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is refused, the incorporating party or agent must file a written reconsideration request to the Director of Corporate Maintenance, Service Alberta, within 30 days of the refusal notice, explaining lawful grounds and, if necessary, submitting a revised NUANS report. A fee may apply. The Director will issue a final administrative decision; a further appeal may be brought to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta by way of judicial review. If the 90-day name reservation expires, a new NUANS report must be commissioned and additional fees paid.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office providing a physical street address within Alberta is permitted for the statutory registered office and records office, and a service provider may accept service of process. However, it is unsuitable if the Alberta entity has no management presence, because the Canada Revenue Agency applies the common law 'central management and control' test to determine corporate residency. For an active cross-border battery-grade lithium carbonate trading company, a co-working suite or professional office address with local staffing is recommended to support GST/HST registration, treaty benefits, and commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Routine inspections by Alberta Corporate Registry are not conducted; however, the physical office may be subject to unannounced inspection visits by bailiffs or process servers for service of process. In approximately 20% of high-risk trade compliance reviews, the Canada Revenue Agency or FINTRAC/RCMP may conduct an on-site inspection in response to suspicious cross-border financial flows. The likelihood is quantified as low-to-moderate: under 10% probability of an on-site inspection in the first 12 months, increasing to 15-25% if enhanced due diligence is triggered by PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, or unusual payment rails.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA) — Part 1 Incorporation (ss. 6-9), Corporate Capacity (Part 2), Registered Office and Records (s. 101), Directors and Officers (ss. 102-155).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Government of Alberta), available through the Corporate Registry online portal or authorized Alberta registry agents.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Alberta Form 1) filed under s. 6 ABCA, accompanied by Consent of Registered Office (Form 3) and Directors' Consents (Form 7); issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation completes incorporation. Government filing fee: CAD 100 plus approx. CAD 7 service charge (approx. USD 75 total at CAD/USD 1.36).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow obligation applies under Alberta law to a wholesale battery-metals arbitrage corporation. Articles may establish one or more classes of shares, including no-par-value common shares, and paid-up capital must not exceed the consideration actually received for the issued shares. A nominal subscription of one common share (CAD 1) is customary.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, as the First Board Resolution: 1. That the incorporators' subscription offers be and hereby are accepted; the Corporation's shares are allotted per the Subscription Schedule and share certificates are issued. 2. That the registered office be and hereby is fixed at [full Alberta address], within the Province of Alberta, where required statutory records shall be maintained. 3. That [Director Names] be and hereby are elected directors by acclamation. 4. That the following officers be appointed until the next annual general meeting: [President], [Secretary], [Chief Financial Officer]. 5. That the officers are authorized to open corporate banking accounts, effect GST/HST and corporate tax registrations, and execute all commercial documents incidental to battery-grade lithium carbonate procurement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Reservation (NUANS Search)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) via Authorized Registry Agent / NUANS service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name search request through an authorized Alberta registry agent and obtain the NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) report. Provide a primary name and two alternatives ending in Corporation, Incorporated, Limited, or the abbreviations Corp., Inc., Ltd. Verify that the proposed name is distinct from existing Canadian corporate and trademark databases. After clearing conflicts, note the NUANS reservation validity of up to 90 days while preparing the articles.
required_dossiers: Completed NUANS search request (online form)
Proposed corporate names (primary and alternates)
Name search fee payment (approx. CAD 25-40, agent-dependent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NUANS report flags a conflicting identical or confusingly similar name, select an alternate name from the same search or adjust the distinctive element; the registry may issue a Name Consent from the conflicting corporation if applicable. Refiling the reserved name within the 90-day window incurs no additional reservation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation (Form 1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) / corporate legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Alberta Form 1 in accordance with ABCA s. 6, setting the corporate name, no-par-value or par-value share structure, maximum number of shares, the number and names of first directors (minimum one; no Alberta residency requirement for directors), and the heading Articles of Incorporation. Execute the articles by the incorporator; secure the registered office consent (Form 3) and each director's written consent (Form 7). Alberta requires a physical registered office address in Alberta, not a post-office-box-only designation.
required_dossiers: Alberta Form 1 - Articles of Incorporation (signed by incorporator)
Consent of Registered Office (Form 3) signed by the registered office holder
Directors' Consents (Form 7) for each initial director
NUANS name search report
Optional subscription agreements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: When the registry or agent identifies a deficiency (e.g., incomplete schedules or missing consents), amend the affected schedule and resubmit through the same portal; no additional incorporation fee is typically charged unless the corporate name or share class changes materially.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles, Fee Payment and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry - online filing window or authorized registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the executed Form 1 with the Alberta Corporate Registry together with Form 3 and Form 7; pay the statutory incorporation fee of CAD 100 plus a small registry service charge (approx. CAD 7). The registry stamps the articles and issues the Certificate of Incorporation, from which date the corporation exists as a separate legal entity (ABCA s. 9). Order a certified registry extract for banking and KYC purposes. Commence the anniversary return calendar for the corporate annual return, due within two months of each incorporation anniversary.
required_dossiers: Completed and executed Form 1
Filed Form 3 and Form 7 consents
Government fee payment receipt
Proof of NUANS report and name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the administration rejects the filing, obtain a formal written rejection note and correct the specified fields; a complete resubmission is processed within one business day. Name-related rejections may require a new NUANS report and a new reservation fee, while purely formal defects are waived if cured within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolutions, Adoption of By-Laws and Corporate Minute Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting (in person or by electronic resolution) and: establish quorum; adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution; approve the by-laws of the corporation; confirm the registered office; allot and issue shares (recording consideration received); appoint officers; open the corporate minute book with Articles, Certificate of Incorporation, by-laws, Register of Directors, Shareholder Register, and the registered office record. Share certificates are signed and delivered to subscribers.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Alberta Form 1 Articles
Signed director and registered office consents
Subscription schedule and share certificates
Approved corporate by-laws
Initial board meeting minutes and resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If defects are identified in allotment (e.g., unpaid subscription consideration), cure the defect by holding a supplementary board resolution and issuing share cancellation or re-allotment promptly before any third party relies on issued share records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number, GST/HST and Income Tax Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Incorporation and the Business Registration Online portal, register the corporation for the federal Business Number (BN) and, to the extent required or beneficial, for the GST/HST account, the T2 corporate income tax account, and any payroll (RP) account if employees later exist. Since the target payment rails are SWIFT LC and wire transfers, register the import/export account with the Canada Border Services Agency and provide banking direct-debit details. As Alberta no longer levies a provincial corporation capital tax, no additional provincial corporate tax account is required.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation or registry extract
First Board resolution and officer appointment minutes
Directors' and officers' identification documents
Corporate postal address and banking details for CRA direct debit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA places the BN under review because of the business purpose code for wholesale battery-metals arbitrage, respond with a resolution and commercial agreement identifying battery-grade lithium carbonate trading (ISIC 4662 / NAICS 423510) and supplier/customer jurisdictions; CRA will confirm the master business record within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence, Banking Rails (SWIFT LC/Wire) and AML/KYB Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary or City of Edmonton Business Licensing; multilateral banks under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the local municipal business licence for the corporate premises (offices and optional warehouse), which requires payment of a local development fee and submission of the lease or occupancy permission. At the banking stage, present the corporate kit to the relationship bank and complete FINTRAC-mandated customer due diligence: UBO verification, source-of-funds declaration, and sanction/PEP screening. Open corporate bank accounts with SWIFT LC advisory and outgoing/incoming wire capabilities; an enhanced monitoring and trade finance screening profile may be placed given the battery-metals arbitrage profile and Medium Risk Enhanced rating.
required_dossiers: Municipal business licence application form
Certificate of Incorporation and certified registry extract
Lease agreement or registered office consent
Shareholder register and UBO declaration (Register of Individuals with Significant Control, if applicable)
Bank KYB/CDD forms and source-of-funds letters
Board resolution approving account signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality questions commodity storage at the premises, present the fire safety letter and a sealed-bag storage limitation protocol, or relocate the warehousing to a zoned industrial property and file a licence amendment. Should a bank decline the account for sector-specific concerns, require a written declination, remediate client questionnaires, and approach a second-tier Schedule I lender with a trade finance desk; adverse bank decisions may be appealed under normal banking ombudsman procedures if discriminatory.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No Alberta provincial industrial licensing authority is triggered because the entity is a merchant wholesaler (NAICS 423510) engaged only in cross-border trade; the passive physical compliance authorities are Alberta Municipal Affairs - Safety Services (Alberta Building Code and Fire Code) and Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) for exempt warehousing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory industrial operating permit is required. The only premises-level document is the Municipal Business Licence from the City of Calgary or Edmonton, plus a Canada Border Services Agency import/export program account for cross-border arbitration of battery-grade lithium carbonate powder.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no EIA registration or approval is required for pure procurement/arbitrage and designated warehouse functions. An EIA Registration under the Activities Designation Regulation (A.R. 228/97) would be triggered only if a lithium carbonate processing, calcination or battery-grade beneficiation plant is later built; no full EIA is contemplated for this scope.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No regulated wastewater, VOC or particulate emissions arise in trading operations. If sealed-bag storage is adopted, keep lithium carbonate in dry form, implement WHMIS and TDG handling protocols, monitor dust loadings to the Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives (PM2.5 24-hour objective of 30 micrograms per cubic metre where ambient compliance is assessed), and manage any spill residue through an AEPA-licensed waste carrier where the Waste Control Regulation applies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code for the leased office/warehouse; occupancy load and structural certification by a licensed engineer if palletized powder loads exceed 500 kg/m2; annual workplace hazard assessment under the Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Act; registration with the Workers' Compensation Board (WCB) if employees are engaged; first-aid kits and spill-containment station placed on-site.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), administered primarily through Business Registration Online and My Business Account. Alberta corporate income tax matters are administered by Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration; Alberta has no general provincial sales tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign corporation should establish its Canadian legal or taxable business presence and obtain a nine-digit Business Number (BN) from the CRA through Business Registration Online, telephone registration, or Form RC1 where applicable. It must provide legal name, incorporation jurisdiction, registered address, directors, business activities, accounting period, and authorized representative information. It should then open the applicable program accounts: RT for GST/HST, RM for import-export activities, RP for payroll if applicable, and RC for corporate income tax where required. A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada, making taxable supplies in Canada, importing commercial goods, or otherwise meeting Canadian registration criteria may require a BN and GST/HST registration. CRA may require supporting incorporation documents, proof of identity, Canadian business information, and security for a non-resident GST/HST registrant. Importers must also obtain a Canada Border Services Agency importer account through the CARM Client Portal and maintain an RM import-export program account. GST/HST registration is generally effective from the date specified by the CRA or the date the statutory registration obligation arises. Provincial corporate registration with the Alberta Corporate Registry is separate from CRA tax registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no general United States-style check-the-box election for corporations. A Canadian corporation is generally a separate taxpayer subject to federal and Alberta corporate income tax on its taxable income. Relevant elections may include a section 85 Income Tax Act rollover for qualifying transfers of eligible property to a taxable Canadian corporation, section 86 share reorganizations, amalgamation and winding-up elections, and treaty-based entity characterization positions where applicable. Canadian hybrid-mismatch rules under sections 12(1)(l.1), 18.4 and related provisions can deny deductions or impose inclusion consequences for deduction/non-inclusion and imported mismatch arrangements. A foreign entity cannot generally elect to be treated as a Canadian flow-through entity merely by filing a classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST), with Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) applying in participating provinces. Alberta applies the federal GST and does not impose a general provincial sales tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies, generally measured over four consecutive calendar quarters or exceeded in a single calendar quarter. A person exceeding the small-supplier threshold must register and begin charging GST at the applicable statutory time. The threshold does not generally exempt a non-resident that is required to register under special rules, including certain non-resident suppliers and persons importing taxable supplies in the course of commercial activities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no general real-time GST invoice-clearance, electronic fiscal-stamping, or mandatory e-invoicing API regime for ordinary business-to-business transactions. Electronic invoices and electronic accounting records are generally acceptable if they contain prescribed information, support the recipient's input tax credit claim, and remain accessible and reliable for the statutory retention period. A GST registrant must generally issue documentary support showing supplier identity and GST/HST registration number, invoice date, transaction description, consideration, applicable GST/HST rate, and tax amount, with enhanced information required for higher-value supplies. CARM electronic customs processes apply to commercial imports, but they are not a GST invoice-clearance system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods supplied in Canada and exported from Canada may generally qualify for zero-rating where the supplier ships or delivers the goods outside Canada, or the purchaser exports them in circumstances satisfying the Excise Tax Act rules. The supplier must retain objective evidence that the goods left Canada and must not treat a Canadian domestic delivery as an export merely because the purchaser is non-resident. Services supplied to a non-resident may qualify for zero-rating where the statutory non-resident and place-of-supply conditions are met, subject to exclusions for services relating to Canadian real property, tangible personal property, litigation, and other specified Canadian activities. Zero-rating does not eliminate customs, export-control, sanctions, dangerous-goods, or import requirements in the destination country. Input tax credits and GST refunds require valid tax documentation, commercial-purpose evidence, and records linking purchases to zero-rated or other commercial activities.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, purchaser or consignee, goods, value, currency, terms, and country of origin

Export declaration or electronic export report through the Canadian Export Reporting System where an export declaration is legally required; certain goods, destinations, values, and controlled goods may be subject to specific reporting rules
Bill of lading, airway bill, carrier manifest, or equivalent transport evidence showing movement from Canada to a destination outside Canada
Packing list and product description, including tariff classification and lithium-carbonate specifications where relevant
Proof of export or delivery outside Canada, such as carrier confirmation, customs exit evidence, or foreign import documentation
Import permits, export permits, certificates of origin, and dangerous-goods documentation where required by the goods, destination, trade agreement, or transport mode
GST/HST sales invoices, contracts, purchase orders, accounting records, and evidence supporting the zero-rated treatment
Evidence of consideration and settlement, such as bank records or payment confirmations; an Inward Remittance Certificate is not generally a Canadian statutory requirement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada does not generally impose a mandatory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. The CRA may reassess GST, deny zero-rating, recover improperly claimed input tax credits or rebates, and charge arrears interest where export conditions or substantiation requirements are not met. False statements or omissions may result in gross-negligence penalties, generally 50% of the related understated tax or improperly claimed amount, and other administrative penalties. Repeated or deliberate non-compliance may lead to criminal prosecution, fines, and imprisonment. Customs non-compliance may trigger CBSA Administrative Monetary Penalty System assessments, seizure or forfeiture, reassessment of duties and taxes, and sanctions for false export or import declarations. Records supporting zero-rated supplies and tax claims must be retained for the applicable Canadian statutory period, generally six years from the end of the relevant tax year.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary and settlement authority; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as prudential bank regulator; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as statutory transaction-reporting agency; Canada has no standalone foreign-exchange-control ministry or exchange-approval regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Canada maintains no exchange-control law, no requirement for profit-remittance licensing, and no limitation on dividend, interest, royalty, or proceeds repatriation for Canadian business corporations. The only statutory gates are (i) Part XIII non-resident withholding tax on outbound remittances (25% statutory rate, treaty-reduced under specific tax treaties, e.g., Canada-U.S. treaty rates of 5-15% for dividends and generally 0-15% for interest/royalties), and (ii) mandatory FINTRAC reporting of international electronic fund transfers of CAD 10,000 or more. Inward and outward capital flows require no Bank of Canada authorization; formalities are limited to bank-level know-your-client checks and corporate-power validation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes zero export-proceeds surrender requirements and zero mandatory conversion ratios. Export receipts may be retained in any freely convertible currency in authorized foreign-currency accounts at Canadian chartered banks. Statutory obligations are confined to (i) customs documentation under the Customs Act and Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) processes, including B13A export declarations where applicable, (ii) FINTRAC prospective reporting of international funds transfers equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000, and (iii) standard corporate record-retention for transfer-pricing and audit evidence. No statutory repatriation timeline exists; commercial receivable terms govern the timing of collection and conversion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD/USD cash management and supplier payment rails)
Capital Escrow Account (temporary hold-for-inbound-injection and share-subscription proceeds)
Operational Account (trade finance and SWIFT MT103 settlement account)
Capital Escrow Account (escrowed funds for border-clearing and LC collateral)
Operational Account (secondary contingency account for CAD clearing)
Operational Account (Alberta-based support account and provincial-funding line)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Conditional Medium. Federally regulated payment-service-provider fintechs registered under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) and restricted-purpose trust companies can be used as secondary pass-through collection accounts. Offshore non-Canadian digital bank and e-money-institution (EMI) accounts are legally constrained: they are not Schedule I/II Canadian banks, do not hold CDIC-insured deposit status, cannot directly access the Lynx (formerly LVTS) high-value clearing system or SWIFT settlement membership, and must themselves register as money services businesses (MSB) with FINTRAC when serving Canadian clients. Use of such EMIs for core treasury is not viable as the primary clearing rail; transactions are limited to small-value supplier onboarding, expense disbursements, and cross-border receivables collection. All funds sweeping from EMIs to the Schedule I primary bank account must be accompanied by source-of-funds and commercial-invoice documentation to avoid enhanced-due-diligence downgrades.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors of a federal or Alberta-incorporated business corporation are NOT required to appear physically at a Canadian bank branch. Remote and online account opening is permitted by all Schedule I banks for domestic corporations under the client-identification rules of the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). For a Medium-Risk Enhanced wholesale trading entity, the standard mandate is (i) a live video-call interview with at least two directors or senior executive officers; (ii) submission of certified true copies of passports and proof-of-address documents, notarized by a public notary or certified by a licensed Canadian lawyer if the individuals are outside Canada; (iii) original or certified Articles of Incorporation, Certificate of Existence/Status, and statutory register of directors; (iv) an Alberta Corporate Registry Company Access Report; (v) a board resolution approving account opening, signing authorities, and account-usage purpose; and (vi) confirmation of registered office and record agent. Physical branch attendance is required only where document certification cannot be completed or where a Relationship Manager assigns a high-risk escalation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder opacity or nominee/offshore holding-structure ambiguity that obscures ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) of the Ontario/Alberta intermediate trading entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation; signed Articles of Incorporation with full share-condition schedule; current Alberta Corporate Registry annual return; complete Register of Directors and Register of Shareholders; notarized UBO declaration identifying every individual owning 25% or more of shares; organizational chart tracing ownership to natural persons; and source-of-wealth statements for each UBO supported by bank statements and asset verification letters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds mismatch for the initial inbound capital injection (expected CAD 500,000 to CAD 2,000,000 wire from a non-Canadian parent or shareholder).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or reviewed financial statements of the funding company; 12-month bank statements showing fund accumulation; signed share-subscription agreement or written shareholder-loan agreement; authenticated board resolution evidencing corporate power; legal opinion from Canadian counsel confirming capacity and authority of the funding entity; and write-off/credit-risk analysis if funds include a shareholder loan subject to deemed-interest rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-documentation mismatch in the wholesale battery-metals supply chain (ISIC 4662 / NAICS 423510), including inconsistent product description for battery-grade lithium carbonate.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contract warehouse pack: purchase orders, proforma invoices, master supply agreement with Incoterms; accredited third-party laboratory assay certificates confirming battery-grade lithium carbonate purity and impurity profile; bills of lading with harmonized TS/HS code 2836.91 declaration and matched cargo weights; CBSA customs entry records; supplier KYC pack including registry extracts, beneficial ownership identification, and sanctions-screening confirmation; and end-use certificates for Canada/OECD electric-vehicle or energy-storage applications.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, export-control, or politically-exposed-person (PEP) red flag on a lithium-carbonate supplier or counterparty with high-risk jurisdiction nexus (e.g., direct or indirect PRC, Russian, or other restricted-country origin).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Licensed sanctions-screening and PEP due diligence report; full supply-chain mapping of upstream producers; written Canadian legal opinion confirming non-application of the Special Economic Measures Act, the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, and the Export Control List; affirmative confirmation of non-controlled end-use; and forwarding documentation demonstrating that the goods remain in Canada or are exported only to treaty-allied OECD purchasers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Short trading history or newly incorporated special-purpose vehicle (SPV) with no prior financial statements or corporate credit history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan with 24-month cash-flow forecast; board-minute packet approving treasury mandates; shareholder support letter or subordinated-debt commitment; trade-finance facility term sheet from an existing Schedule I bank relationship; personal or parent-company guarantee where permissible; and a committed central treasury policy that routes all settlement through the Canadian account to avoid shell-like disintermediation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing is via SWIFT MT103 (customer transfer) or MT202 (bank-to-bank) from the home-country bank into the CAD or USD settlement account held at the Canadian Schedule I bank. The payment must include a full purpose-code statement in field 70, e.g., capital contribution to Canadian subsidiary for working capital, so that the receiving bank can satisfy FINTRAC reporting of international electronic fund transfers of CAD 10,000 or more. Supporting documentation must be uploaded to the bank treasury portal same-day: board resolutions, share-subscription or shareholder-loan agreements, and beneficial-ownership declarations. If the capital is in USD or RMB, conversion into CAD is executed as an ordinary spot transaction on the bank treasury desk; no Bank of Canada permit or administrative approval is required. A shareholder loan received inbound should be evidenced by a written agreement bearing an arms-length prescribed-rate or market-rate coupon to avoid deemed-interest and Canadian withholding-tax characterizations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails are (i) SWIFT MT103 for non-documentary supplier settlements in USD, EUR, or offshore RMB, settled domestically via Lynx (formerly LVTS) for the CAD leg and via Fedwire/CHIPS for the USD leg through the bank's US correspondents; (ii) documentary irrevocable letters of credit (UCP 600) issued by the Canadian Schedule I bank and confirmed by a prime overseas bank for battery-grade lithium carbonate imports, with full transport-document and assay-compliance requirements; (iii) standby letters of credit (ISP98) for performance, advance-payment, or customs-bond obligations; and (iv) documentary collections for low-exposure, repeat suppliers. All outbound wires of CAD 10,000 or more are FINTRAC-reportable and must be supported by commercial invoices, supplier contracts, customs-entry documentation, and truthful purpose codes. Trade-settlement records, LC schedules, and bill-of-lading matrices must be retained for seven years to demonstrate economic substance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forwards (deliverable, up to 24-month tenors) in CAD-USD executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Credit Support Annex collateralized with the sponsoring Schedule I bank treasury
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in CNH/offshore RMB and other hard-to-deliver currencies to hedge Chinese-supplier procurement exposure where no local RMB clearing account is maintained
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (MTM-collateralized) converting USD or RMB trade-finance liabilities into CAD floating-rate obligations linked to CORRA

European-style FX options (premium-paid, zero-premium strangles) to hedge contingent price volatility in multi-currency lithium-carbonate supply off-takes, complemented by index-linked commodity forwards referenced to published battery-grade lithium carbonate assessment prices

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 100 late filing penalty; failure to file for one year triggers administrative dissolution by Corporations Canada.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee up to CAD 100; failure to file for three consecutive years initiates administrative strike-off of the corporation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Individual with Significant Control (ISC) Register Attestation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Alberta Corporate Registry (maintained on-site; attesting information filed with annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the federal and Alberta annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with ISC register maintenance may result in fines up to CAD 5,000 and prohibition on individuals acting as directors; escalating to administrative dissolution if annual returns are persistently omitted.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to distributing corporations and corporations without unanimous shareholder waiver; non-distributing private corporations may dispense with an audit by unanimous shareholder consent under CBCA/ABCA. No revenue or asset monetary threshold applies to private non-distributing corporations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable and distributing enterprises; Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for eligible non-distributing private corporations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Maintain a register of individuals with significant control (ISC) under CBCA/ABCA and update it within 15 days of any change in significant-control interests; confirm accuracy of ISC information during each annual return filing. The register is not publicly filed but must be available to law enforcement and prescribed officials upon demand.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% (federal 15% Part I corporate rate + Alberta 8% general rate; combined headline rate for a non-resident-controlled trading corporation)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The combined 13% small-business rate (9% federal + 4% Alberta) on the first C$500,000 applies only to Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs). A corporation controlled by non-residents is not a CCPC; therefore no SBD is available. The Alberta 6% M&P rate does not apply to wholesale procurement/distribution. No statutory tax holiday applies; the federal clean technology investment tax credit (30%) is inapplicable to pure trading. Effective combined rate is 23%.
